title: Digital Foundry Reveals Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave: 720p Docked, 540p Handheld, 30fps, DLSS Support
body:
The latest installment of the long‑running Fire Emblem franchise, *Fortune’s Weave*, has become the focal point of a detailed technical review by Digital Foundry, the video‑game performance lab known for dissecting hardware limits. Their findings reveal that the title runs at a modest 720p in docked mode and 540p on the handheld screen of the newly released Nintendo Switch 2, capped at 30 frames per second, yet it incorporates Nvidia’s DLSS upscaling technology—a surprising blend of Nintendo’s portable hardware and high‑end PC graphics tricks.

The analysis shows that while the resolution figures may appear underwhelming compared to other contemporary releases on the platform, the implementation of DLSS (Deep Learning Super Sampling) helps to retain visual fidelity despite the lower native pixel count. By feeding a lower‑resolution image through an AI‑driven upscaler, the game can produce sharper textures and smoother edges without taxing the Switch 2’s GPU beyond its 30 fps ceiling. This marks the first time the console’s hardware has been confirmed to support DLSS, a feature traditionally reserved for Nvidia’s RTX line of graphics cards, and suggests a deeper partnership between Nintendo and Nvidia than previously evident.

From a performance standpoint, the 30 fps lock is a deliberate design choice rather than a limitation. The developers appear to have prioritized stable frame timing and consistent visual quality over chasing the 60 fps benchmark that many modern titles aim for. In a genre where strategic planning and narrative immersion take precedence over reflex‑based action, a steady frame rate can actually enhance readability of the battlefield and reduce eye strain during long play sessions. Moreover, the 720p docked output still surpasses the original Switch’s typical 720p ceiling, indicating that the upgraded SoC in the Switch 2 delivers a modest but meaningful bump in raw processing power.

Critics and players alike have noted that *Fortune’s Weave* feels like a natural evolution of the series’ aesthetic, blending classic sprite‑style units with modern lighting and particle effects. The DLSS implementation appears to smooth out jagged edges on character models and terrain, giving the game a polished look that belies its handheld origins. However, the 540p handheld resolution may still be noticeable on the device’s 7‑inch screen, especially for gamers accustomed to the sharper 1080p output of competing handhelds. Digital Foundry’s benchmarks indicate that the upscaled image retains sufficient detail for most players, but the experience could feel less crisp when viewed up close.

The technical breakdown also sheds light on Nintendo’s broader strategy for the Switch 2. By integrating DLSS, the company signals an openness to leveraging third‑party AI technologies to extend the lifespan of its hardware without a radical redesign. This approach mirrors the industry trend of using software‑based upscaling—such as AMD’s FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) and Intel’s XeSS—to bridge the gap between hardware constraints and consumer expectations. For Nintendo, the move could allow future titles to push visual boundaries while staying within the power envelope of a portable console, preserving battery life and thermal headroom.

Looking ahead, the success of DLSS on *Fortune’s Weave* may set a precedent for upcoming Switch 2 releases, particularly those in graphically intensive genres like action‑RPGs and open‑world adventures. If developers can reliably harness AI upscaling without sacrificing performance, the platform could see a wave of visually richer experiences that were previously thought impossible on a handheld. For now, the combination of respectable 720p docked performance, stable 30 fps gameplay, and AI‑enhanced graphics positions *Fire Emblem Fortune’s Weave* as a benchmark title, illustrating how Nintendo’s next‑gen console can balance legacy design philosophies with cutting‑edge technology.
